protections: Unsafe git option guard: Git.check_unsafe_options over Git._option_candidates must see every option spelling that will reach the git command line (git/cmd.py:973-1047), applied at clone (git/repo/base.py:1458-1464), archive (git/repo/base.py:1680-1684), ls-remote (git/cmd.py:1117-1119), fetch/pull/push (git/remote.py:1073-1077, 1130-1134, 1206-1210) and revision walkers (git/repo/base.py:823-826, 1135-1138, 1242-1246; git/objects/commit.py:340-343).
Blocklists of command-executing / file-writing options per git subcommand (git/repo/base.py:145-176, git/remote.py:538-553, git/cmd.py:652-655, git/objects/commit.py:90-93).

evidence: git/cmd.py:1716-1720 (the caller's kwargs, including split_single_char_options, are passed straight into transform_kwargs, which accepts it as its own parameter at git/cmd.py:1616)
git/cmd.py:1605-1608 (split_single_char_options=False joins name and value into one '-<k><v>' token)
git/cmd.py:1042-1046 (_option_candidates emits only '-<k>' for a single-char kwarg and ignores the value and the split mode)
git/cmd.py:1008 (n, q, v, f, l, s, 4, 6 are treated as clusterable before -u/-c, but the checker never sees the joined token)
git/repo/base.py:145-152 (-u and -c are the blocked clone short options)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: the report names clone and -u; archive's -o writes a file rather than running a command
evidence: git/repo/base.py:164-170 (archive blocks -o / --output / --exec)
git/repo/base.py:1680-1684 (archive guard uses the same _option_candidates([], kwargs))
git/repo/base.py:1691 (kwargs, including split_single_char_options, go to git.archive)
git/cmd.py:1008 (v and l are clusterable, so a joined '-v'+'o<path>' token would be caught only if the checker saw it)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: a fix that simulates the joined token for scalar values looks complete
evidence: git/cmd.py:1620-1622 (list/tuple values of a single-char kwarg are each joined into separate tokens)
git/cmd.py:1043-1046 (candidate collection only tests whether any list element is truthy and emits one bare '-<k>')

traps.reason_to_dismiss: the clusterable set lists git's value-less flags, and widening it would wrongly reject safe attached values such as -oupstream
evidence: git/cmd.py:1005-1008 (the clusterable set is '46flnqsv' only)
git/cmd.py:1025-1026 (the cluster walk stops at the first character outside that set)
git/repo/base.py:164-170 (archive blocks -o; git archive's compression-level flags -0..-9 are value-less short flags, and only 4 and 6 are in the set)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: --upload-pack is already blocked for ls-remote, and --exec looks like a push-only option
evidence: git/cmd.py:652-655 (the ls-remote blocklist holds only --upload-pack)
git/remote.py:548-553 (--exec is blocked only for push)
git/cmd.py:1029-1033 (prefix matching only catches abbreviations of listed names, so an alias name that is not listed passes)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: diff is a read-only comparison; 'other' is documented as a tree-ish, and kwargs are developer-chosen flags such as R=True
evidence: git/diff.py:188-277 (Diffable.diff has no check_unsafe_options call and no allow_unsafe_options parameter)
git/diff.py:263-266 (a string 'other' is inserted into argv before the '--' separator)
git/diff.py:271-273 ('--' is added only when paths are given)
git/diff.py:277 (all kwargs, including split_single_char_options, are forwarded to git diff / diff-tree)
git/repo/base.py:172-176 and git/objects/commit.py:90-93 (--output / -o are treated as unsafe for the sibling revision commands)
test/test_diff.py:470 (commit.diff(..., split_single_char_options=False, M='75%') must keep working)
test/test_diff.py:484 (the same with M='40%')
test/test_git.py:199-202 (joined safe short values -oupstream and -bcurrent must pass)
test/test_clone.py:226-237 (clone with -oupstream must succeed)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: env is a documented, caller-trusted parameter (Repo.clone_from env=), not a git option
evidence: git/cmd.py:76-89 ('env' is an execute kwarg and is separated from the options at git/cmd.py:1713)
git/cmd.py:1368-1378 (the inline env is merged into the subprocess environment)
git/cmd.py:1046 (the guard sees it only as '--env', which is not on any blocklist)
git/repo/base.py:1577 and git/repo/base.py:1594-1600 (env is a documented clone_from parameter)

masking: T4 is reachable only through joined single-char kwargs (split_single_char_options=False, git/cmd.py:1608). archive takes kwargs only (git/repo/base.py:1682), so T4 matters only after T1 is fixed by making _option_candidates emit the joined token. A T1 fix that rejects or normalises split mode makes T4 unreachable.

conflicts.what: Rejecting or stripping split_single_char_options=False in _call_process/_option_candidates (git/cmd.py:1720) breaks diff(..., split_single_char_options=False, M='75%') (test/test_diff.py:470,484).
A new diff guard that refuses joined short tokens or the split flag breaks the M='75%' similarity diff, which needs '-M75%' as one token (git/cmd.py:1608, test/test_diff.py:470).

Widening the cluster walk to scan every character (git/cmd.py:1025-1026) rejects -oupstream / -bcurrent (test/test_git.py:199-202, test/test_clone.py:231). Only the value-less digit flags may be added.
A T1 fix that rejects any joined single-char kwarg containing 'u' or 'c' breaks legitimate joined values such as o='upstream' or b='current' under split mode.

fairness_risks: split_single_char_options=False is a public, tested knob (test/test_diff.py:470,484). A rule that forbids it, rather than inspecting the joined token, contradicts must-keep-working behaviour.
Joined safe short values (-oupstream, -bcurrent) must stay allowed (test/test_git.py:199-202, test/test_clone.py:231). A rule that treats 'u' or 'c' anywhere in a short token as unsafe is unfair.
T8: env= is a documented clone_from parameter (git/repo/base.py:1577,1594-1600). A hidden test that requires blocking GIT_CONFIG_* in env contradicts documented API and should not be used.
T6: Diffable.diff has no allow_unsafe_options parameter today (git/diff.py:188-194). A test must not require a specific escape-hatch name unless the report states it.

design.why: Fixing the advisory route correctly at the shared candidate builder closes T1 and T2 together, while a fix local to _clone leaves archive open. T6 is the strongest deepseek-type trap: there is no guard at all, a plausible 'read-only diff' reason to dismiss it, and it is one file away from the report. T5 is a second, independent deepseek-type trap with a different dismissal ('upload-pack is already blocked'). T7 is the mimo-type coupled value: split_single_char_options=False with M='75%' and -oupstream must keep working, which punishes over-hardening of T1 and T6. Each trap has its own fix site and its own reason to dismiss. T4 is left out because T1 masks it, and T8 is left out because a documented API makes it unfair.

unverified: A fix e8d0fbf774d1 and B fix 96a888f4d782 were not inspected (no git history access with the tools used). That A added the joined/cluster short-option walk (git/cmd.py:1005-1026) is inferred from tests test/test_git.py:186-197 and the 3.1.51 changelog (doc/source/changes.rst:29-33). Whether B lives in A-authored lines (b_in_code_a_wrote) is not determined.
Whether the published B fix is central (_option_candidates / _call_process), and therefore also covers archive (T2), or is local to clone was not checked.
T5 depends on git's ls-remote accepting a hidden '--exec' alias for --upload-pack (builtin/ls-remote.c). This is git binary behaviour that cannot be checked in this repository.
T6 depends on git diff / diff-tree accepting --output=<file> (a common diff option). This was not confirmed against the installed git.
T4 depends on git archive's -0..-9 compression flags being clusterable short flags (e.g. '-9o<path>' parsed as -9 -o <path>). This is git binary behaviour and was not checked.

Whether rev-list / blame accept a short '-o' was not checked; if they do not, the revision-walker members of the T2 family are not exploitable and the -o entries at git/repo/base.py:175 and git/objects/commit.py:92 are defensive only.
The T8 exploit shape (GIT_CONFIG_COUNT / GIT_CONFIG_KEY_n via env=) is git behaviour and was not run.
